tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings

Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

schema.name: ToolSearch
schema.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

lines: +Run everything from the project folder, in PowerShell:
+Every command starts with `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe`, the project's Python. This sheet shortens that to `py`. To type `py` for real, run this once in each new terminal:

+**How to read an option:** `--until N` means you type `--until` and then a value in place of `N`, for example `--until 2`. Each table says what the value is, its units, and what happens if you leave the option out (the **default**). An option with no value, such as `--live`, is a switch: writing it turns it on. Options can go in any order.

+**Run one command at a time.** The camera tools and the controls editor keep the terminal busy until you close them. A second pasted line waits until then, or sits at the prompt until you press Enter. To run two at once, open a second terminal (the **+** in VS Code's terminal panel), or start the editor in the background:
+Only one tool can listen to a glove at a time. Close one (`q`, F9 or the window) before starting the next.
+| 1. Flash the glove (only if its WiFi or IP changed) | `py flash.py cam --ip auto` |
+| Part | Value | Default | What it does |

+| `BOARD` (required, no `--`) | `cam`, `s3`, `cam-check` or `s3-check` | none | Which board and sketch. **cam** = ESP32-CAM glove (`firmware/glove_imu`). **s3** = ESP32-S3 glove (`firmware/glove_imu_s3`). **cam-check** / **s3-check** = sensor checks that use USB only, with no WiFi |

+| `--ip ADDRESS` | An IP address such as `172.20.10.5`, or `auto` for this laptop's current WiFi address, or `""` to broadcast | Leaves `config.h` as it is | Which computer the glove sends its data to. Saved into the board's `config.h` before building. Broadcasting loses about a third of the data, so give one address |

+| `--ssid NAME` | The WiFi network's name, in quotes if it has spaces or an apostrophe: `--ssid "Andre's iPhone"` | Leaves `config.h` as it is | Which WiFi network the glove joins. The password is not set here: edit `config.h` for that, so it never ends up in your terminal history |
+| `--port COMn` | A serial port name such as `COM6` | Found automatically | Which USB port the board is on. Only needed if it picks the wrong one; `--list` shows them |
+| `--seconds N` | Seconds (decimals allowed) | `12` | How long to show the board's own messages after flashing. `0` skips this |
+| `--watch` | switch | off | Don't flash; just show the board's messages (for `--seconds` seconds) |
+| `--list` | switch | off | List the USB serial ports and stop |
+Examples: `py flash.py cam --ip auto`, `py flash.py cam --ip 172.20.10.5 --ssid "Andre's iPhone"`, `py flash.py cam --watch --seconds 30`.
+- The ESP32-CAM flashes on its programmer board, where the sensor isn't connected, so "Sensor 0 Hz" there is normal. Move it to the breadboard afterwards.
+- Look for `Sending UDP to <this laptop's IP>`.
+- If the ESP32-S3 won't connect, hold BOOT, tap RST, let go of BOOT, and run the command again.
+**cam-check result**, on the red LED once on the breadboard:
+- a short blink each second: the sensor is alive
+- a slow blink: it was found, but its data is bad
+- a fast flicker: no sensor found
+## `glove_check.py`: is the glove sending good data?
+It runs four steps in order and tells you what to fix:
+1. Hear the glove: any data arrives at all.
+2. Data quality: frames arrive intact, at the right rate, with few gaps.
+3. At rest: hold the glove still. Gravity should read 1 g, and rotation near 0.
+4. Punches: throw a few, and each is counted with how hard it hit.
+| Option | Value | Default | What it does |
+| `--until N` | Step number: `1`, `2`, `3` or `4` | `4` (all steps) | Stop after step N. `--until 2` = just "is data arriving, and how fast" |
+| `--wait N` | Seconds | `45` | How long step 1 waits for the glove before giving up |
+| `--port N` | UDP port number | `5005` | `5005` = left glove, `5006` = right glove |
+| `--hz N` | Samples per second | `500` | The rate the firmware should send. Step 2 compares against it |
+| `--punches N` | Number of punches | `5` | How many punches step 4 asks for |
+| `--punch-seconds N` | Seconds | `30` | How long step 4 waits for those punches |
+| `--simulate` | switch | off | Use a fake glove, to try the tool |
+`py glove_receiver.py` shows the glove's live numbers, including whether the button reads `HELD`. Its only option is `--simulate`.
+- In the camera window, **C** calibrates: a 5 s countdown, then stand in guard.
+- **.** (full stop) starts, and pauses or resumes. It works from any window.
+- In the terminal, `x` + Enter undoes the last saved punch, and `q` + Enter quits.
+| Option | Value | Default | What it does |
+| `--target N` | Number of each punch | `100` | Stop when every punch type has N recordings. **Recordings you already have count**: with 20 saved, `--target 40` records 20 more |
+| `--person NAME` | Any word, such as `andre` | empty | Who is punching. Saved with each recording, for your own records |
+| `--arm SIDE` | `left` or `right` | `left` | Which glove. `right` uses port 5006 and saves to `punch_data_right/` |
+| `--button` | switch | off | Old mode: hold the glove button around each punch instead of following beeps. Records no NONE examples |
+| `--data FOLDER` | A folder path | `punch_data` (left), `punch_data_right` (right) | Where to save the recordings |
+| `--windowed` | switch | off (full screen) | Start in a normal window. F11 switches while running |
+| `--camera N` | Webcam number | `0` (the built-in one) | Use another webcam: `1`, `2`, ... |
+| `--port N` | UDP port number | The arm's: `5005` or `5006` | Listen for the glove on another port |
+| `--max-seconds N` | Seconds | none (runs until done) | Stop by itself after N seconds (for testing) |
+| `--simulate` | switch | off | Fake glove, no hardware |
+**NONE examples:** in "MOVE, DON'T PUNCH" rounds, move sharply (snap your guard, feint, bob). Each one saved shows `saved NONE n` in the terminal.
+**Where recordings go:** `punch_data/<PUNCH>/`. Folders starting with `_` are ignored: `_rejected` holds failed attempts, and `_old_mpu6050` the old sensor's data.
+| Option | Value | Default | What it does |

+| `--features WHICH` | `both`, `imu` or `pose` | `both` | What the model learns from: glove and camera (`both`), glove only (`imu`), or camera only (`pose`). Accuracy for all three is printed either way |
+| `--arm SIDE` | `left` or `right` | `left` | Which glove's recordings and model |
+| `--data FOLDER` | A folder path | The arm's folder | Train on other recordings |
+| `--out FILE` | A file path ending in `.joblib` | `models/punch_rf.joblib` (left) | Where to save the model. `punch_live.py --model FILE` plays with it |
+| `--config FILE` | A settings file | `punch_config.json` | Which punch settings to cut the recordings with |
+| Option | Value | Default | What it does |
+| `--live` | switch | off (dry run) | Really press keys. Without it, it only prints them. With it, key output starts OFF: press **F8** |
+| `--windowed` | switch | off (full screen) | Camera in a normal window. F11 switches |
+| `--popup` | switch | off | Camera as a small always-on-top window in a corner, so the game stays visible |
+| `--popup-corner WHERE` | `bottom-right`, `bottom-left`, `top-right` or `top-left` | `bottom-right` | Which corner the popup sits in |

+| `--confidence N` | A number from 0 to 1 (`0.7` = 70%) | `0.6`, from `punch_config.json` | How sure the model must be before it presses a key. Higher = fewer wrong keys but more missed punches. **[** and **]** change it while playing |
+| `--start-g N` | g (1 g = gravity) | What the model was trained with (2.5) | How hard a movement must be to count as a punch. Change it by 1 or less, or retrain |
+| `--no-tracking` | switch | off | Ignore the glove button: no mouse steering, and the normal keys always |
+| `--mapping FILE` | A controls `.json` file | `mappings/controls.json` | Which keybinds to use |
+| `--arm SIDE` | `left` or `right` | `left` | Which glove and model |
+| `--model FILE` | A `.joblib` model | The arm's model | Play with another model |
+| `--camera N` | Webcam number | `0` | Use another webcam |
+| `--port N` | UDP port number | `5005` / `5006` | Listen on another port |
+| `--max-seconds N` | Seconds | none | Stop by itself (for testing) |
+| `--simulate` | switch | off | Fake glove, no hardware |

+**Tracking mode:** hold the glove button, and your right hand steers the mouse from where it was when you pressed. Punches then use the tracking binds (default: jab = left click, hook = right click, uppercut = middle click). The camera's block is off while you hold the button.
+`py punch_live_both.py` runs both gloves' models at once. It takes `--live`, `--windowed`, `--confidence N`, `--camera N`, `--mapping FILE`, `--max-seconds N` and `--simulate`, which work as above.
+| Option | Value | Default | What it does |
+| `--mapping FILE` | A controls `.json` file | `mappings/controls.json` | Which file to edit. A new name creates it from the defaults |
+**Binding a key:** click a bind, then press a key or click a mouse button. Esc cancels, and **x** clears the bind.
+**Hold (ms)** is how long a punch keeps its key or mouse button down, in milliseconds.
+| Speed / Position | Speed acts like a thumbstick: holding the hand out keeps turning. Position acts like a trackpad: the view follows the hand | Speed |
+| Speed (px/s) | Pixels per second, with the hand half a shoulder-width from where it started | 1200 |
+| Curve | 1 = even; higher = finer control near the centre, faster at the edge | 1.5 |
+| Dead zone | How far the hand can drift without moving the mouse, in shoulder widths | 0.06, about 2 cm |
+| Sensitivity (position mode) | Pixels per shoulder-width of hand movement | 1500 |
+| Vertical vs horizontal | Up/down speed compared with left/right. 0.5 = half as fast | 1.0 |
+| Invert up/down | Flips the up/down direction | Off |
+| Camera BLOCK works while tracking | Lets block work while you steer | Off |
+Changes save straight away, and a running `punch_live.py` picks them up within a second.
+| Command | Value | Default | What it does |
+| `py punch_settings.py` | none | none | Show every setting |
+| `timeout N` | Milliseconds, 100 to 1500 | `350` | The longest a punch can last before it is cut off. The key is pressed when the punch ends, so shorter = less delay. **Retrain afterwards** |
+| `confidence N` | 0 to 1 | `0.6` | The default confidence cutoff for `punch_live.py`. No retraining needed |
+| `start_g N` | g | `2.5` | How hard a movement must be to start a punch. Retrain afterwards |
+| `decel_g N` | g | `3` | How hard a stop must be to end a punch early |
+| `pre_s N` | Seconds | `0.25` | How much movement before the start is included, such as an uppercut's dip |
+| `lag N` | Seconds | `0` | How far the camera runs behind the glove |
+Other names are listed by `py punch_settings.py`. Every tool reads these settings when it starts, so restart any tool that is open.
+## `punch_tune.py`: watch punches being found, and pick a timeout
+`py punch_tune.py`. It takes the same `--arm`, `--windowed`, `--camera N`, `--port N`, `--max-seconds N` and `--simulate` options as above.
+Type these in its terminal, each followed by Enter:
+| `N` (just a number, such as `300`) | Milliseconds | Try that timeout. You see each punch's start and end on screen |

+| `test N S PUNCH` (such as `test 10 60 jab`) | N = how many punches, S = seconds to throw them in, PUNCH = `jab`, `hook` or `uppercut` | A timed test. Press **.** to start. At the end it shows how many punches it found and how they were classified, at this timeout and several others |
+| `py -m unittest discover tests` | Run every test, on fake data; no hardware needed |

+| `py controller.py --live` | Kadir's older camera-only controller. `--glove` only accepts punches the glove also felt; `--simulate-glove` uses a fake glove; `--builtin-punches` uses the original punch rules; `--mapping FILE` |
+| `py game_input.py --live` | Presses every mapped key once after a 5 s countdown, to test that the game receives them |
| Low-confidence predictions press no key | The model only knows three classes, so other movement must not be forced into one of them |

| A second arm is optional and fully separate (2026-11-07) | The right glove uses port 5006, its own data folder, model and punches (CROSS, HOOK, UPPERCUT), selected with `--arm right`. The left arm keeps its original data and model, and stays the default. Camera features are mirrored for the right arm |

| The glove sends to one laptop's address, not broadcast (2026-11-07) | Broadcast over the phone hotspot lost about a third of the samples, in gaps of up to about 350 ms, enough to swallow a whole punch. Sending to one address gets WiFi's automatic re-sends. To use another computer, flash its address |

+| Tracking mode on the glove button (2026-11-07) | Holding the button turns the right hand into a mouse joystick (camera, right wrist relative to the right shoulder, from where it was at the press), and switches punches to a tracking set of binds (default: mouse clicks, held 150 ms). The camera's BLOCK is off while tracking, because the steering hand sits near the face; duck and slip stay on. Speed and position steering are both available. Binds live in `mappings/controls.json` (normal, tracking and defence sets) and are edited with `controls_editor.py`; `browser_boxing.json` keeps the older format, which still loads |

+| Recordings save the live gravity estimate (2026-11-07) | NONE examples happen while moving, so the saved slice never shows the glove still, and a fresh punch finder (which waits for stillness) found nothing: every NONE was rejected. Capture now saves `start_gravity`, and capture and training start the punch finder from it |
| Separate live script, `controller.py` left unchanged | Keeps Kadir's rule-based controller as a demo fallback |

+| A phone can be the right arm's sensor instead of a glove (2026-11-07) | The phyphox app serves the phone's accelerometer and gyroscope and the laptop polls it (`phyphox_imu.py`). It is chosen with `--phone ADDRESS` together with `--arm right` in `punch_capture.py`, `punch_tune.py` and `punch_live.py`, or `--right-phone` in `punch_live_both.py`, and is refused for the left arm so the left glove's recordings and model can't be mixed with it. Polling means nothing has to connect into the laptop: in testing, a phone's connection into the laptop never arrived (from a teammate's hotspot or an iPhone's own), while the laptop reaching the phone worked. The right arm's recordings, model and punches stay as for the right glove. A phone has no magnetometer and reports about 80 to 100 Hz against a glove's 500 Hz. Capture's "enough data" check used to assume 500 Hz and rejected every phone recording as dropped packets (shown as MISSED); it now scales with the sensor's measured rate (`LiveSensors.sample_rate_hz`). A browser-page alternative (`phone_imu.py`) is kept but did not work in that test |
| `punch_live.py` | Classifies punches live and presses keys |
| `punch_sim.py` | Fake glove data that follows the punch definitions. Used by `--simulate` and the tests. It shows the code runs, not that the model works on real punches |
+| `hand_aim.py` | Tracking mode: right-hand steering of the mouse while the glove button is held |
| `punch_live_both.py` | Runs the left and right models side by side, with one camera |
**Status (2026-11-07):** all of the above is built and tested on simulated data. The firmware compiles but hasn't been flashed. Nothing has been tested on real punches yet.

+**Right arm from a phone:** `phyphox_imu.py` polls the phyphox app and plugs into `LiveSensors` through `--phone` (with `--arm right`). The receiver has run on a real phone (about 80 to 100 Hz). 60 right-arm punches (20 each of CROSS, HOOK and UPPERCUT) were recorded with it, and `models/punch_rf_right.joblib` was trained on them: 98% cross-validated, but from one session, so optimistic. It has no NONE (not a punch) examples yet and has not been tried live. `phone_imu.py` with `phone/index.html` is a browser-page alternative that did not work (see the decision above).

**Shared parts:** `glove_receiver.py`, `pose_tracker.py`, `game_input.py`, `firmware/glove_imu/` (the left glove, ESP32-CAM). `firmware/glove_imu_s3/` is an ESP32-S3 glove for either arm, and `firmware/mpu6050_usb_check/` and `firmware/mpu9250_usb_check/` check whether a sensor is alive over USB.

**Earlier work, kept and not the main path:** `controller.py`, `glove_punch.py`, `punch_detector.py`, `tune_punches.py`, `replay_punches.py` (Kadir's camera-rules controller), `glove_check.py` (still the first thing to run if the glove seems broken), `punch_tracker.py`, `firmware/punch_stream/`, `firmware/sketch_nov6a/` (wired Uno experiments).
## Main pipeline: glove and camera with a trained model
+Every command and option is listed in [COMMANDS.md](COMMANDS.md). Flash the boards from the terminal with `python flash.py cam` (or `s3`, `cam-check`, `s3-check`).
| 1. Check the glove | `python glove_check.py`, then `python glove_receiver.py` | Confirms data arrives. The receiver also shows whether the button reads `HELD` |
| 4. Train | `python punch_train.py` | Trains the random forest and reports glove-only, camera-only and combined accuracy. Saves `models/punch_rf.joblib` |

| 5. Play | `python punch_live.py --live` | J jab, H hook, U uppercut, plus W/S/A/D defence keys from the camera. F7 calibrate, F8 key output, F9 quit. **[** and **]** lower or raise the confidence cutoff while playing, with no retraining. `--confidence 0.7` and `--start-g 3` set the cutoff and the punch threshold at startup. `--popup` shows the camera as a small always-on-top window in a screen corner (`--popup-corner`, `--popup-size`) that never takes focus from the game and ignores clicks, so quit with F9. A game in exclusive full screen hides it |

+**Tracking mode and keybinds.** Hold the glove button (GPIO12 to GND) and your right hand steers the mouse like a joystick, from where it was when you pressed. **What was on the branch (committed and pushed last session):**
- **Tracking mode:** while you hold the glove button, your right hand works the mouse like a joystick, starting from where it was when you pressed. Jab presses the left mouse button, hook the right and uppercut the middle. The camera's block is off while you steer.
- **Keybind window:** `controls_editor.py` edits `mappings/controls.json` (normal, tracking and defence sets). Saved changes apply to a running `punch_live.py`.
- **NONE fix:** "not a punch" examples were always being rejected. Recordings now save the gravity estimate so they get through.
- **"NO GLOVE DATA":** shows once, in red.
- **Flashing from the terminal:** `flash.py` builds and flashes each board, without Arduino IDE.
- **`COMMANDS.md`:** every command and option, with values, units and defaults.
- **Left arm retrained:** on the 60 new MPU-6500 punches (100% cross-validated). The old MPU6050 recordings were moved to `punch_data/_old_mpu6050`.

**What I did today:**
- Kadir merged PR #11 (the phone as the right arm's sensor) after your branch was pushed, and it changed some of the same code in `punch_capture.py`. I kept both changes: your saved gravity estimate and its check that adjusts for the phone's lower sample rate.

- I pushed the merge to `origin/andre/tracking-mode`. It is 2 commits ahead of `main` with no conflicts.

**State of the project:**
- **Left arm (ESP32-CAM glove + webcam):** recorded and trained, and live classification was nearly perfect when you tested it.
- **Right arm (phone):** a first model exists, but it has no NONE examples and hasn't been tried live.
- **Tracking mode and the keybind window:** tested only on simulated data, not with real punches yet.

**Next:**
1. Open the PR and get Kadir's approval.
2. Record NONE examples for the right arm and retrain it.
3. Try tracking mode in a real game.

Every tool except training takes `--simulate`, which uses a fake glove so you can try it without hardware. Run the tests with `python -m unittest discover tests`. The supporting modules are `punch_segment.py` (finds where punches start and end), `punch_features.py` (turns a punch into model inputs), `punch_session.py` (shared buffers, settings and data files) and `punch_sim.py` (fake glove data, for testing only). Shared settings live in `punch_config.json`.
The other scripts below came earlier and still work: Kadir's rule-based camera controller, and the wired Uno tracker.

To tell two gloves apart, add their IP addresses to `GLOVE_BY_IP`. Any glove not listed is treated as `L`. If the sensor is mounted at an angle, set `AXIS_MAP` and `AXIS_SIGN`.

Receives a phone's accelerometer and gyroscope as the right-hand sensor, by polling the free phyphox app. The laptop opens the connection to the phone, so nothing has to get through the laptop's firewall. On the phone, open the printed `https://<laptop address>:8443` in Safari or Chrome, accept the certificate warning, tap Start and allow motion access. Keep the page open and the screen on. Windows Firewall (and Norton, if it is on) must allow inbound TCP on port 8443. If the phone lying flat with the screen up reads -1 g on z, run with `--flip-accel`. If rotation looks about 57 times too small, add `--gyro-rad`. Set `AXIS_MAP` and `AXIS_SIGN` for how the phone sits on the hand. Samples use the glove id `R` and the same units as `glove_receiver.py`, and the left glove's pipeline does not see them. Nothing finds or classifies right-hand punches yet.

+# Shelved: one webcam, boxer turned 45 degrees

+One webcam, with the boxer turned about 45 degrees to it and the lead (left) shoulder toward the camera. At that angle a straight punch moves partly across the picture, so jabs and crosses can be seen. A front-on camera cannot see them.

+Straight punches and uppercuts held up. Hooks did not: a flat right hook from the guard looks the same as a cross, and a left hook that arcs upward looks like an uppercut. lines: -# Project brief: read this before changing anything

-The team's agreed plan. Every agent and teammate works from it. If your task conflicts with it, stop and ask rather than quietly changing direction. If the team changes a decision, update this file in the same pull request.

-1. **Check for new work:** run `git fetch origin`, then `git log --oneline HEAD..origin/main` and `git branch -r`. Read anything that touches your files. Teammates merge often, so a file list from earlier in a session can be out of date.
-2. **Check the Brain:** run `entire brain brief "<task>" --json` and `entire brain recall "<question>" --json` for earlier decisions and known problems.
-3. **Check the code:** follow `.entire/agent-guide.md` and use Graph to find what depends on the code you'll change.

-4. **Branch from an up-to-date `main`:** name it `yourname/what-youre-building`. Never commit straight to `main`. It is protected, so work reaches it through a pull request, and Kadir must explicitly approve a merge to `main`. Before any push or merge, say what the source and target are.
-5. **Agree who owns a file** before editing a teammate's file.

-6. **Record what you learn:** use `entire brain remember "<memory>" --path <category.subcategory.type> --kind <decision|gotcha|...> --json` for anything durable the code doesn't state, and update this file if the plan changes.
-Claude Code also gets an automatic notice of new `main` commits and open branches with each prompt, from `.claude/hooks/sync_check.sh`. Other agents must run step 1 themselves.
-A left-hand boxing controller. A motion sensor on the glove and a webcam watch a punch, a model decides whether it was a jab, hook or uppercut, and the laptop presses a key to control a boxing game.
-1. **Glove:** an ESP32-CAM reads an MPU6050 and streams raw data over WiFi using UDP, at 500 Hz.
-2. **Network:** the ESP32 and laptop share a phone hotspot (2.4 GHz). Set `LAPTOP_IP` in `config.h` to the laptop's address on the hotspot, and allow Python through the Windows firewall.

-3. **Camera and sync:** the laptop runs pose estimation on webcam frames (OpenCV captures, MediaPipe estimates the pose). IMU samples and frames are both timestamped on the laptop clock so they can be matched up.

-4. **Finding a punch:** a punch starts on high acceleration. It ends at a selectable timeout or on high deceleration, whichever comes first. `punch_tune.py` sets the timeout and shows starts and ends live on the pose display. Its timed test (`test 10 60 jab`) counts and classifies the punches thrown in one minute, at the current timeout and at several others for comparison.

-5. **Classifying:** a random forest uses features from the IMU and from joint angles. Only if that isn't good enough, try a small neural network on the raw sensor data (Google Colab or Gemini tools are options, undecided).
-6. **Output:** each punch becomes a key press. Defence keys from the camera stay on.
-Left hand only. Features and data collection depend on these definitions:
-| Left hook | Left, then forward, then right | `H` |
-| Uppercut | Arm moves down, then up | `U` |
-Defence keys: block `W`, duck `S`, slip left `A`, slip right `D`. These are in `mappings/browser_boxing.json`.

-Record **100 jabs, 100 left hooks and 100 left uppercuts** with `punch_capture.py`. By default the screen calls each punch with a beep, in random order. The strongest punch in the next 1.6 s gets that label. Movement caught between prompts, plus a "MOVE, DON'T PUNCH" round every 15 prompts, is saved as **NONE** (not a punch), so the model learns to press nothing for guard adjustments and feints. The original button mode is still available as `--button`: hold, punch, release.
-| Random forest first, neural network only if needed | Works with 300 examples and is quick to test |
-| Always store raw data, then compute features afterwards | Lets us change the timeout and features without recording again |
-| The same punch-finding code runs in training and live | The button only sets the label and time range, because no button exists during play |

-| Webcam straight in front of the boxer | Team choice, and easy to set up. A front camera barely sees a straight punch, so jabs rely mostly on the glove. Training reports glove-only, camera-only and combined accuracy |
-| Button on GPIO12, wired to GND | GND wiring can't pull this boot-sensitive pin high. **Never connect GPIO12 to 3V3**, or the board won't boot |
-| Button state travels in the frame's second sync byte: `A5 5A` released, `A5 5B` pressed | Every frame carries it, so a lost packet can't lose a press, and firmware without a button still works |
-| Deceleration only ends a punch once the arm settles | Uppercuts and hooks reverse direction mid-punch, and a reversal also looks like high deceleration |

-| Calibration waits 5 seconds after C or F7, with an on-screen countdown | Design rule: gives the boxer time to get into guard, or to click back into the game, before the stance is recorded. Applies to every tool built on `pose_tracker.py`, through `CALIBRATE_DELAY_S` |

-| Training is prompted by a timer, not the button (2026-11-07) | Holding a button changes your grip and fist compared with play, and the timer naturally collects not-a-punch examples. The button stays as `--button` |
-| A fourth class, NONE, for movement that isn't a punch | Anything the punch finder catches reaches the model in play. Without NONE, every guard adjustment would become a jab, hook or uppercut |

-| Sensitivity is adjustable without retraining | The confidence cutoff comes from `punch_config.json` or `--confidence`, not the model, and the [ and ] keys change it while playing (not F5/F6, which reload a browser game). `--start-g` moves the punch threshold, but only small changes are safe; big ones need a retrain. The timeout always needs a retrain |
-| Low-confidence predictions press no key | The model only knows three classes, so other movement must not be forced into one of them |

-| A second arm is optional and fully separate (2026-11-07) | The right glove uses port 5006, its own data folder, model and punches (CROSS, HOOK, UPPERCUT), selected with `--arm right`. The left arm keeps its original data and model, and stays the default. Camera features are mirrored for the right arm |

-| The glove sends to one laptop's address, not broadcast (2026-11-07) | Broadcast over the phone hotspot lost about a third of the samples, in gaps of up to about 350 ms, enough to swallow a whole punch. Sending to one address gets WiFi's automatic re-sends. To use another computer, flash its address |

-| Tracking mode on the glove button (2026-11-07) | Holding the button turns the right hand into a mouse joystick (camera, right wrist relative to the right shoulder, from where it was at the press), and switches punches to a tracking set of binds (default: mouse clicks, held 150 ms). The camera's BLOCK is off while tracking, because the steering hand sits near the face; duck and slip stay on. Speed and position steering are both available. Binds live in `mappings/controls.json` (normal, tracking and defence sets) and are edited with `controls_editor.py`; `browser_boxing.json` keeps the older format, which still loads |

-| Recordings save the live gravity estimate (2026-11-07) | NONE examples happen while moving, so the saved slice never shows the glove still, and a fresh punch finder (which waits for stillness) found nothing: every NONE was rejected. Capture now saves `start_gravity`, and capture and training start the punch finder from it |
-| Separate live script, `controller.py` left unchanged | Keeps Kadir's rule-based controller as a demo fallback |

---
name: esp32-flashing-workflow
description: "How Andre flashes the glove ESP32-CAM (programmer board on COM6, then moved to the breadboard) and the upload command that works"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: dc26e6a1-c62f-47c2-89e2-b1ac6a6ea252
  modified: 2026-11-07T18:57:40.571Z
---

The glove's AI Thinker ESP32-CAM is flashed on a CH340 programmer board over USB (showed up as COM6 on 2026-11-07), then removed and plugged into the breadboard with the MPU6050 and button. While on the programmer board the sensor and button are NOT connected, so serial shows "Sensor 0 Hz, N read errors" — expected, not a fault. Hardware tests (glove_check.py, button HELD) only work once it is back on the breadboard, over WiFi.

Upload that works: `"C:\Program Files\Arduino IDE\resources\app\lib\backend\resources\arduino-cli.exe" compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32cam --upload --port COM6 firmware/glove_imu` (esp32 core 3.3.12). Read serial with pyserial at 115200 with dtr/rts set False before opening, or the programmer board holds the chip in reset.

ESP32-S3 glove (firmware/glove_imu_s3): plugs straight in by USB-C, native USB shows as COM3 (VID 303A). Build with FQBN `esp32:esp32:esp32s3:CDCOnBoot=cdc` or nothing prints on that port. To read its startup log, reset with the bundled esptool `--after watchdog-reset chip-id`, then reopen COM3 in a retry loop (the port drops during reset).

Network: phone hotspot "Andre's iPhone" since 2026-11-07 afternoon (was "Andrew Saweras"; iPhone, laptop got 172.20.10.4, teammate's laptop 172.20.10.5, ESP32-CAM 172.20.10.3, S3 172.20.10.2; Windows marks it Public). Broadcast (LAPTOP_IP "") loses about a third of samples there, so always flash a specific IP. On eduroam the glove can't connect at all. config.h (gitignored) holds the SSID/password and LAPTOP_IP; the laptop IP can change on reconnect. See [[group-git-workflow]].

---
name: esp32-flashing-workflow
description: "How Andre flashes the glove ESP32-CAM (programmer board on COM6, then moved to the breadboard) and the upload command that works"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: dc26e6a1-c62f-47c2-89e2-b1ac6a6ea252
  modified: 2026-11-07T18:57:40.571Z
---

The glove's AI Thinker ESP32-CAM is flashed on a CH340 programmer board over USB (showed up as COM6 on 2026-11-07), then removed and plugged into the breadboard with the MPU6050 and button. While on the programmer board the sensor and button are NOT connected, so serial shows "Sensor 0 Hz, N read errors" — expected, not a fault. Hardware tests (glove_check.py, button HELD) only work once it is back on the breadboard, over WiFi.

Upload that works: `"C:\Program Files\Arduino IDE\resources\app\lib\backend\resources\arduino-cli.exe" compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32cam --upload --port COM6 firmware/glove_imu` (esp32 core 3.3.12). Read serial with pyserial at 115200 with dtr/rts set False before opening, or the programmer board holds the chip in reset.

ESP32-S3 glove (firmware/glove_imu_s3): plugs straight in by USB-C, native USB shows as COM3 (VID 303A). Build with FQBN `esp32:esp32:esp32s3:CDCOnBoot=cdc` or nothing prints on that port. To read its startup log, reset with the bundled esptool `--after watchdog-reset chip-id`, then reopen COM3 in a retry loop (the port drops during reset).

Network: phone hotspot "Andre's iPhone" since 2026-11-07 afternoon (was "Andrew Saweras"; iPhone, laptop got 172.20.10.4, teammate's laptop 172.20.10.5, ESP32-CAM 172.20.10.3, S3 172.20.10.2; Windows marks it Public). Broadcast (LAPTOP_IP "") loses about a third of samples there, so always flash a specific IP. On eduroam the glove can't connect at all. config.h (gitignored) holds the SSID/password and LAPTOP_IP; the laptop IP can change on reconnect. See [[group-git-workflow]].

---
name: esp32-flashing-workflow
description: "How Andre flashes the glove ESP32-CAM (programmer board on COM6, then moved to the breadboard) and the upload command that works"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: dc26e6a1-c62f-47c2-89e2-b1ac6a6ea252
  modified: 2026-11-07T22:37:44.243Z
---

The glove's AI Thinker ESP32-CAM is flashed on a CH340 programmer board over USB (showed up as COM6 on 2026-11-07), then removed and plugged into the breadboard with the MPU6050 and button. While on the programmer board the sensor and button are NOT connected, so serial shows "Sensor 0 Hz, N read errors" — expected, not a fault. Hardware tests (glove_check.py, button HELD) only work once it is back on the breadboard, over WiFi.

Upload that works: `"C:\Program Files\Arduino IDE\resources\app\lib\backend\resources\arduino-cli.exe" compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32cam --upload --port COM6 firmware/glove_imu` (esp32 core 3.3.12). Read serial with pyserial at 115200 with dtr/rts set False before opening, or the programmer board holds the chip in reset.

ESP32-S3 glove (firmware/glove_imu_s3): plugs straight in by USB-C, native USB shows as COM3 (VID 303A). Build with FQBN `esp32:esp32:esp32s3:CDCOnBoot=cdc` or nothing prints on that port. To read its startup log, reset with the bundled esptool `--after watchdog-reset chip-id`, then reopen COM3 in a retry loop (the port drops during reset).

Gotcha: the iPhone hotspot name uses a CURLY apostrophe (Andre’s iPhone, U+2019, UTF-8 E2 80 99). A straight ' in config.h WIFI_SSID means the glove never joins (no UDP, not in arp). Check with PowerShell `Get-NetConnectionProfile` (netsh wlan shows nothing here).

Network: phone hotspot "Andre’s iPhone" since 2026-11-07 afternoon (was "Andrew Saweras"; iPhone, laptop got 172.20.10.4, teammate's laptop 172.20.10.5, ESP32-CAM 172.20.10.3, S3 172.20.10.2; Windows marks it Public). Broadcast (LAPTOP_IP "") loses about a third of samples there, so always flash a specific IP. On eduroam the glove can't connect at all. config.h (gitignored) holds the SSID/password and LAPTOP_IP; the laptop IP can change on reconnect. See [[group-git-workflow]].

content.text:
The glove is now sending over WiFi. The check passed:

- **Connection:** the laptop is receiving from the glove, which got the address 172.20.10.5 on the hotspot this time.
- **Data:** 498 frames a second, with the sensor at its expected 500 Hz. There were no lost frames, no junk bytes and no gaps over 50 ms.

The missing battery was probably why the glove didn't show up at all. I changed the WiFi name at the same time, so I can't tell whether the curly apostrophe also mattered. I've added both to my notes.

The glove is ready for `punch_capture.py`, `punch_tune.py` or `punch_live.py` on port 5005. One thing to remember: you're still on `main`, so tracking mode and the other new features only arrive once the pull request is merged, or after `git switch andre/tracking-mode`.

+2. Data quality: frames arrive intact, at the right rate, with few gaps.
+3. At rest: hold the glove still. Gravity should read 1 g, and rotation near 0.
+4. Punches: throw a few, and each is counted with how hard it hit.

+Every command and option is listed in [COMMANDS.md](COMMANDS.md). Flash the boards from the terminal with `python flash.py cam` (or `s3`, `cam-check`, `s3-check`).

| 4. Train | `python punch_train.py` | Trains the random forest and reports glove-only, camera-only and combined accuracy. Saves `models/punch_rf.joblib` |

| 5. Play | `python punch_live.py --live` | J jab, H hook, U uppercut, plus W/S/A/D defence keys from the camera. A game in exclusive full screen hides it |

+**Tracking mode and keybinds.** Hold the glove button (GPIO12 to GND) and your right hand steers the mouse like a joystick, from where it was when you pressed. Up and down move the view up and down; left and right move it left and right. While the button is held, punches use a second set of binds (by default jab = left click, hook = right click, uppercut = middle click, each held 150 ms), and the camera's block is off so a raised steering hand can't trigger it. Duck and slip still work. `python controls_editor.py` opens a keybind window with three sets: normal (button up), tracking (button held) and defence (camera). Click a bind, then press a key or click a mouse button. The window also chooses the steering style: speed (like a thumbstick) or position (like a trackpad), and how fast. Changes save to `mappings/controls.json` at once, and a running `punch_live.py` picks them up within a second. `--no-tracking` ignores the button.

**Two gloves (optional).** Everything above is the left arm, and it is the default. A second glove on UDP port 5006 is the right arm: add `--arm right` to `punch_tune.py`, `punch_capture.py`, `punch_train.py` and `punch_live.py`. The right arm has its own recordings (`punch_data_right/`), model (`models/punch_rf_right.joblib`) and punches (CROSS = K, HOOK = H, UPPERCUT = U; its hook goes right, forward, left). Its camera features are mirrored, so a hook looks the same to both models. `python punch_live_both.py --live` runs both models side by side with one camera, and an arm with no model yet is left off. `glove_check.py --port 5006` checks the right glove. A glove with a magnetometer also gets magnetometer features. This is tested on simulated data only.

The camera tools open full screen. **F11** switches to a window and back, so you can reach the terminal, and `--windowed` starts in a window. Timed sessions never start on their own: calibrate with **C** (a 5-second countdown into guard), then press **.** (full stop, from any window) to start. Press **.** again to pause or resume. This covers the tuner's `test` and the capture session.

+This was one of the three product versions in `variants/README.md`. The team chose the front camera plus glove instead (`PROJECT.md`), so this one is parked here. Nothing in the project loads it. The code is complete and was working when it was shelved.

+One webcam, with the boxer turned about 45 degrees to it and the lead (left) shoulder toward the camera. At that angle a straight punch moves partly across the picture, so jabs and crosses can be seen. A front-on camera cannot see them.
+Measured on two full recordings (36 punches each) at a true 45 degrees, with the settings in `settings.json` and nothing changed between sessions:

+Straight punches and uppercuts held up. Hooks did not: a flat right hook from the guard looks the same as a cross, and a left hook that arcs upward looks like an uppercut. Retuning on one session and testing on the other gave no reliable gain, so the weakness is in what a single camera can see, not in the settings.

The two-arm test is running in dry-run mode, so it shows which key each punch would press but doesn't press anything.

**What's running:**
- **Left arm:** the glove on port 5005, using the model trained on today's 60 punches from the new sensor.
- **Right arm:** the phone at 172.20.10.1, using its model trained on 60 punches.
- **Keys:** left jab J, left hook H, left uppercut U, right cross K. A right hook and right uppercut get no key of their own in this mapping, so they'll show as detected but press nothing.

I used 172.20.10.1 for the phone rather than 172.25.19.247. It's the same phone, but my first attempt at the address you gave timed out, and 172.20.10.1 is its address on the hotspot, which should stay the same.

I also switched you to `andre/tracking-mode`. `main` still has the old left model from the burned-out sensor, so the left arm would have classified badly there.

**To test:**
1. In the camera window, press **C**, then get into guard. It counts down 5 seconds before calibrating.
2. Throw a few of each punch with each arm and watch what it labels them.
3. Press **F9** to quit, then tell me how it went and I'll go through the output.

The right arm has never seen "not a punch" examples, so it will probably label guard adjustments as punches. That's expected for now.

def build_dataset(root, config, quiet=False, side="L"):
    """Returns (X, y, groups, names, skipped). side is the arm the camera features look at."""
    rows, labels, groups, skipped = [], [], [], Counter()
    seg_settings, lag = config["segment"], config["camera_lag_s"]
    for path in ps.block_paths(root):
        block = ps.load_block(path)
        meta, imu = block["meta"], block["imu"]
        segments = punch_segment.find_segments(imu["t"], imu["accel"], imu["gyro"], seg_settings,
                                               meta.get("start_gravity"))  # recorded while moving: NONE
        seg, _ = punch_segment.pick_block_segment(segments, meta["press_t"], meta["release_t"])
        if seg is None or seg.reason == "gap":
            skipped["no punch found with the current settings"] += 1
            continue
        feats = punch_features.extract(imu, block["pose"], seg, seg_settings.pre_s, lag, side=side)
        if feats is None:
            skipped["too little glove data"] += 1
            continue
        rows.append(feats)
        labels.append(meta["label"])
        groups.append(meta.get("session", "?"))
    if not rows:
        return None, None, None, None, skipped
    names = list(dict.fromkeys(n for r in rows for n in r))  # every feature any block has (e.g. magnetometer)
    X = np.array([[r.get(n, np.nan) for n in names] for r in rows], dtype=float)
    return X, np.array(labels), np.array(groups), names, skipped

class Classifier:
    """The random forest saved by punch_train.py, with the punch settings it was trained with.

    min_confidence (how sure the model must be to press a key) is NOT fixed by training: it comes from
    the argument, else from punch_config.json, so it can be changed without retraining.
    """

    def __init__(self, path=MODEL_PATH, min_confidence=None):
        import joblib
        bundle = joblib.load(path)
        self.model, self.features = bundle["model"], bundle["features"]
        self.model.n_jobs = 1  # one punch at a time: starting worker threads costs more than it saves
        self.labels = list(bundle["labels"])
        known = punch_segment.SegmentSettings().to_dict()
        old = sorted(set(bundle["segment"]) - set(known))
        if old:  # a model trained before a setting was removed (e.g. stop_ratio, 2026-11-07)
            print(f"Note: this model has settings that no longer exist and are ignored: {', '.join(old)}. Retrain to update it.")
        self.segment = punch_segment.SegmentSettings.from_dict({k: v for k, v in bundle["segment"].items() if k in known})
        self.camera_lag_s = bundle.get("camera_lag_s", 0.0)
        self.side = bundle.get("side", "L")  # models from before the right glove are left-arm models
        self.min_confidence = load_config()["min_confidence"] if min_confidence is None else float(min_confidence)
        self.info = {k: bundle.get(k) for k in ("trained_at", "counts", "cv_accuracy", "feature_set", "arm")}

    @staticmethod
    def exists(path=MODEL_PATH):
        return os.path.exists(path)

    def classify(self, imu, pose, seg, pre_s=None):
        """(label, confidence) for one punch, or (None, 0.0) if there is too little glove data."""
        import punch_features

content.text:
That test wasn't a good read on either model, partly because the phone was in your left hand for the first half.

**Results from the second half (after you swapped):**
- **Left glove:** never sure enough to press a key. Its best guesses were 36–47%, against the 60% cutoff, and spread across jab, hook and uppercut.
- **Right phone:** mostly labelled punches as CROSS, and was sure enough to press K three times. With only 20 examples per punch and no "not a punch" examples, that's about what to expect.

**The models themselves are fine.** On the merged code, both still label their own training recordings 100% correctly, at about 95% confidence. So the problem is that live punches look different from the recorded ones. The two likeliest reasons:

1. **No calibration.** Nothing in the output shows calibration ran, so it probably didn't. About a third of each model's features come from the camera and are measured against your calibrated guard stance. Without calibration they're off, which pulls every guess toward an even split like the one above.
2. **The glove may have shifted.** If the board or sensor moved on your hand while you fixed the battery, the motion readings won't match the training recordings either.

**Next test:** run the left arm alone, calibrated, with punches thrown in a known order, so we can tell which reason it is:

```powershell
python punch_live.py --windowed
```

1. Press **C** in the camera window, get into guard and wait for the 5-second countdown.
2. Throw 5 jabs, 5 hooks, then 5 uppercuts, with a pause between each.
3. Press **F9** and tell me.

If it's still unsure after calibrating, the glove has probably moved. The fix then is to record a fresh set of about 20 of each punch with `punch_capture.py` and retrain, which takes about 10 minutes. After that, we'll do the same for the right arm, adding NONE examples.

1	"""Record labelled training punches.
2	
3	  python punch_capture.py --person andre               prompted (default): the screen calls the punch
4	  python punch_capture.py --target 20 --person andre   a smaller set, for a first test
5	  python punch_capture.py --button                     hold the glove button around each punch instead
6	  python punch_capture.py --simulate                   fake glove (no hardware), to try the tool
7	
8	PROMPTED MODE (default). Nothing starts until you have calibrated (press C, get into guard during the
9	5 s countdown) and pressed "." (works from any window). "." also pauses and resumes at any time.
10	The screen shows "JAB!", "HOOK!" or "UPPERCUT!" with a beep, in random order.
11	Throw that punch once, then return to guard. The strongest punch in the next 1.6 s gets that label.
12	Anything the punch finder catches while you are NOT being prompted is saved as NONE, a "not a punch"
13	example. Every 15 prompts there is a "MOVE, DON'T PUNCH" round: shuffle, adjust your guard, feint,
14	bob. These NONE examples teach the model to press nothing for movement that is not a punch.
15	Your hands stay as they will be in play, so the training punches match the game.
16	
17	BUTTON MODE (--button). Hold the glove button, throw one punch, release. Collects no NONE examples.
18	
19	Keys that work in any window, no Enter needed:
20	  .       prompted mode: start, then pause or resume at any time
21	  F11     full screen on or off (it starts full screen; --windowed starts in a window)
22	Type in THIS TERMINAL, then Enter:
23	  p       pause or resume (prompted mode), the same as "."
24	  x       undo the last saved punch (moves it to the arm's _rejected/ folder)
25	  j/h/u   button mode only: switch to JAB / HOOK / UPPERCUT
26	  q       quit (everything saved so far is kept); q in the camera window also works
27	
28	The data stays on this computer in punch_data/<LABEL>/ (or punch_data_right/ with --arm right).
29	Train with python punch_train.py (add --arm right for the right arm).
30	"""
31	import argparse
32	import os
33	import random
34	import shutil
35	import sys
36	import threading
37	import time
38	
39	import punch_segment
40	import punch_session as ps
41	
42	NONE = "NONE"
43	PRE_S, POST_S = 1.0, 0.3       # data kept before and after each block
44	MIN_HOLD_S, MAX_HOLD_S = 0.15, 8.0
45	REST_S, GO_S, LATE_S = 1.6, 1.6, 0.6   # prompted: guard, punch window, grace after the window
46	FREE_EVERY, FREE_S, ANNOUNCE_S = 15, 15.0, 4.0
47	GREEN, RED, ORANGE, GREY, YELLOW = (0, 220, 0), (0, 0, 255), (0, 150, 255), (190, 190, 190), (0, 255, 255)
48	TONES = {"JAB": 880, "CROSS": 880, "HOOK": 660, "UPPERCUT": 520, "FREE": 300}
49	
50	
51	def beep(kind):
52	    if sys.platform != "win32":
53	        return
54	    import winsound
55	    threading.Thread(target=winsound.Beep, args=(TONES.get(kind, 700), 120), daemon=True).start()
56	
57	
58	class Capture:
59	    """Shared by both modes: counting, saving and checking blocks, undo, and the terminal."""
60	
61	    def __init__(self, sensors, config, target, root, person, arm=None):
62	        self.sensors, self.config, self.target, self.root, self.person = sensors, config, target, root, person
63	        self.arm = arm or ps.ARMS["left"]
64	        self.how = self.arm.how
65	        self.keys = {label[0].lower(): label for label in self.arm.labels}  # j or c, h, u
66	        self.counts = ps.count_blocks(root, self.arm.labels)
67	        self.counts.setdefault(NONE, 0)
68	        self.saved = []              # (path, label) saved this session, for undo
69	        self.session = time.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
70	        self.result, self.result_colour, self.result_t = "", GREY, 0.0
71	        self.quit = False
72	        self.calibrated = False  # set by pose_tracker after C and its 5 s countdown
73	
74	    def on_calibrated(self):
75	        self.calibrated = True
76	
77	    def remaining(self):
78	        return {k: max(0, self.target - self.counts.get(k, 0)) for k in self.arm.labels}
79	
80	    def say(self, text, colour=GREY):
81	        print(text)
82	        self.result, self.result_colour, self.result_t = text, colour, time.time()
83	
84	    def read_terminal(self):
85	        while not self.quit:
86	            try:
87	                self.command(input().strip().lstrip("\ufeff").lower())  # a byte-order mark
88	            except EOFError:
89	                return
90	
91	    def command(self, word):
92	        if word == "x":
93	            self.undo()
94	        elif word in ("q", "quit"):
95	            self.quit = True
96	        elif word:
97	            self.say(self.HELP)
98	
99	    def undo(self):
100	        if not self.saved:
101	            self.say("nothing to undo")
102	            return
103	        path, label = self.saved.pop()
104	        folder = os.path.join(self.root, "_rejected")
105	        os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
106	        shutil.move(path, os.path.join(folder, "undone_" + os.path.basename(path)))
107	        self.counts[label] -= 1
108	        self.say(f"undid the last {label} ({self.counts[label]})", ORANGE)
109	
110	    def save_block(self, label, t0, t1, quiet=False):
111	        """Check and save the data around [t0, t1] as one block. Returns the punch Segment or None."""
112	        imu, pose = self.sensors.window(t0 - PRE_S, t1 + POST_S)
113	        settings = self.sensors.settings
114	        problem, segment, found, gravity = None, None, 0, None
115	        # At least 60% of the samples the sensor normally sends: its real rate (about 500 Hz for the glove, about
116	        # 100 Hz for a phone), so a slower sensor is not mistaken for dropped packets.
117	        if len(imu["t"]) < 0.6 * self.sensors.sample_rate_hz() * (t1 - t0 + PRE_S + POST_S):
118	            problem = "too little glove data arrived (WiFi dropping?)"
119	        else:
120	            gravity = self.sensors.gravity_at(imu["t"][0])
121	            segments = punch_segment.find_segments(imu["t"], imu["accel"], imu["gyro"], settings, gravity)
122	            segment, found = punch_segment.pick_block_segment(segments, t0, t1)
123	            if segment is None:
124	                problem = "no punch found"
125	            elif segment.reason == "gap":
126	                problem = "the glove data had a gap during the punch"
127	        meta = {"label": label, "arm": self.arm.name, "press_t": t0, "release_t": t1, "session": self.session, "person": self.person,
128	                "mode": self.MODE, "segment_settings": settings.to_dict(), "problem": problem,
129	                "segments_found": found, "pose_frames": int(len(pose["t"])),
130	                "start_gravity": None if gravity is None else [float(v) for v in gravity]}
131	        if problem:
132	            ps.save_block(label, imu, pose, meta, self.root, rejected=True)
133	            if not quiet:
134	                self.say(f"NOT SAVED: {problem}", RED)
135	            return None
136	        path = ps.save_block(label, imu, pose, meta, self.root)
137	        self.saved.append((path, label))
138	        self.counts[label] = self.counts.get(label, 0) + 1
139	        return segment

211	        self.phase, self.phase_end, self.prompt = "waiting", None, None
212	        self.prompts_done, self.paused = 0, False
213	        self.windows = []        # (label, start, end) of every punch prompt, to tell punches from NONE
214	        self.pending = []        # (label, start, end) prompts waiting for their data
215	        self.free = []           # (start, end) of MOVE, DON'T PUNCH rounds
216	        self.none_pending = []   # Segments to save as NONE once their data has arrived

219	        word = word.strip(".")  # "." works in every window, so it may also be typed into the terminal
220	        if word == "p":
221	            self.toggle()
222	        else:
223	            super().command(word)

225	    def not_ready_reason(self):
226	        if not self.sensors.glove_ok():
227	            return "no glove data"
228	        if not self.sensors.segmenter.ready:
229	            return "hold the glove still for a moment"
230	        if not self.calibrated:

234	    def toggle(self):
235	        """The "." key: start, pause or resume."""
236	        now = time.time()
237	        if self.phase == "done":
238	            return
239	        if self.phase == "waiting" or self.paused:
240	            reason = self.not_ready_reason()
241	            if reason:
242	                self.say(f"cannot start yet: {reason}", ORANGE)
243	                return
244	            self.paused = False
245	            self.phase, self.phase_end = "announce", now + ANNOUNCE_S
246	            self.say("starting" if not self.prompts_done else "carrying on", GREEN)
247	            return
248	        # pause: a prompt that is showing right now is cancelled, so it does not count as missed
249	        if self.phase == "go" and self.pending and self.pending[-1][1] >= now - GO_S:
250	            self.pending.pop()
251	            self.windows.pop()
252	            self.prompts_done -= 1
253	        if self.phase == "free":
254	            self.free.append((self.free_start, now))
255	        self.paused = True
256	        self.say("PAUSED - press . to carry on", ORANGE)

266	            left[label] -= 1
267	        bag = [k for k, n in left.items() for _ in range(n)]

272	            if self.phase == "free":
273	                self.free.append((self.free_start, now))
274	            if self.prompts_done and self.prompts_done % FREE_EVERY == 0 and self.phase == "go":
275	                self.phase, self.phase_end, self.free_start = "free", now + FREE_S, now
276	                beep("FREE")

279	            if self.prompt is None:

286	            self.windows.append((self.prompt, now, now + GO_S))
287	            self.pending.append((self.prompt, now, now + GO_S))
288	            self.prompts_done += 1

292	        return any(start - 0.2 <= t <= end + LATE_S for _, start, end in self.windows)

301	        recording = self.phase in ("announce", "rest", "go", "free") and not self.paused
302	        while not self.sensors.events.empty():
303	            kind, value = self.sensors.events.get()
304	            if kind == "end" and value.reason != "gap" and recording and not self.in_prompt_window(value.start_t):
305	                self.none_pending.append(value)

309	        wait = self.sensors.settings.timeout_s + POST_S
310	        for item in [p for p in self.pending if latest >= p[2] + wait]:

318	                         f"{seg.peak_g:.1f} g", GREEN)

320	            self.none_pending.remove(seg)

322	                where = "while moving freely" if any(a <= seg.start_t <= b for a, b in self.free) or self.phase == "free" else "between prompts"
323	                print(f"saved NONE {self.counts[NONE]} (a movement {where})")
